title: Executive Summit: Roadmap Synopsis & Decisive Asks for Quarterly Planning
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Purpose: Create a concise, decision-oriented packet for the Executive Summit that summarizes the proposed 2026-Q2 roadmap, maps features to OKRs, surfaces risks and dependencies, and enumerates exact executive decisions/approvals required.

Scope: Focus on initiatives that materially affect inference economics, Dedicated/Private rollout cadence, and Console observability investments. Exclude low-touch backlog grooming items; include only items with active engineering or compliance workstreams.

Deliverables:
- 1 page executive synopsis (TL;DR with 3 bullets of impact & ask)
- 6-slide appendix covering: roadmap by initiative (commitments & contingencies), OKR alignment, cost/latency impact analysis, top 5 risks and mitigation plan, rollout timeline, and resourcing ask.
- Decision matrix listing the binary asks for exec approval (e.g., approve Dedicated commit increase, greenlight Private pilot expansion to APAC, approve 90-day runway for Optimize feature team).

Key metrics to surface: projected token cost delta vs baseline, P95 tail latency vs SLO, expected Dedicated throughput uplift, Canary failure budget, and projected incremental ARR from enterprise commitments.

Stakeholders: PM (Maya Chen), Platform Eng Lead (Diego Alvarez), Serving Runtime (Rina Patel), Reliability (Owen Kim), Design (Sofia Martinez), Revenue Ops (Priya Nair).

Success criteria: Packet accepted by Execs with clear decisions recorded and at most two follow-up clarifications required. Roadmap items that require immediate resourcing are assigned within 7 calendar days of the summit.

Constraints & trade-offs noted:
- Longer Dedicated capacity lead times (6–8 weeks) vs need for predictable enterprise SLAs — propose phased commitments with rollback triggers.
- Aggressive batching optimizations could reduce unit token cost but increase memory footprint on smaller instances; propose A/B rollout with QA guardrails.
- Private deployment expansion to APAC implies increased compliance and KMS integrations; flag for legal review if approved.
